payload.task_text:
Hey, the finance team needs a comprehensive tax compliance audit for our online store. We have a Tax_Regulations.pdf in your workspace along with a guide.md that explains the methodology, so please review those first.

Pull all order data from the store, including each order's total, tax collected, and billing state. Also pull the configured tax rates. Using the methodology in the PDF and guide, compute the expected tax for every order by matching the billing state to the applicable rate. Remember that if no state-specific rate exists, the default rate with an empty state field should be used as a fallback. If a state has multiple rates configured, sum them together.

Create an Excel file called Tax_Compliance_Report.xlsx in your workspace with three sheets.

The first sheet should be called "Order Tax Audit" with columns Order_ID, Order_Total, Billing_State, Applicable_Rate, Expected_Tax, Actual_Tax, Discrepancy, and Status. Discrepancy is Actual minus Expected. Status is determined from abs(Discrepancy) using inclusive lower-bound rules: when abs(Discrepancy) <= 0.50 mark Compliant (exactly 0.50 counts as Compliant); when 0.50 < abs(Discrepancy) <= 1.00 classify by sign of Discrepancy (positive -> Over-Collection, negative -> Under-Collection, the boundary 1.00 counts here); when abs(Discrepancy) > 1.00 classify by sign in the same direction (positive -> Over-Collection, negative -> Under-Collection). The only non-strict boundary is abs == 0.50 which stays Compliant. Include all orders sorted by Order_ID. Round monetary values to 2 decimals, rates to 4 decimals. All values in the workbook must be written as literal numbers (rounded as specified); do not write Excel formulas.

The second sheet should be called "State Summary" with columns State, Order_Count, Total_Revenue, Total_Expected_Tax, Total_Actual_Tax, Net_Discrepancy, Compliance_Rate_Pct, and Requires_Filing. Sort by state alphabetically. Compliance_Rate_Pct is the percentage of orders within tolerance rounded to 1 decimal. Requires_Filing is Yes if total actual tax exceeds $100, otherwise No.

The third sheet should be called "Compliance Overview" with two columns Label and Value containing summary metrics: Total_Orders_Audited, Compliant_Orders, Over_Collection_Orders, Under_Collection_Orders, Total_Over_Collected, Total_Under_Collected, Net_Tax_Discrepancy, States_Requiring_Filing, and Overall_Compliance_Rate.

Schedule four quarterly tax filing deadline reminders on the calendar as all-day events. Use the dates from the regulations PDF for the year 2026: April 15 titled "Tax Filing Deadline - Q1", July 15 titled "Tax Filing Deadline - Q2", October 15 titled "Tax Filing Deadline - Q3", and January 15 titled "Tax Filing Deadline - Q4".

Create a Google Form titled "Vendor Tax Information" to collect tax details from our vendors. It should have five questions: vendor name as a short text field (free-form), tax ID number as a short text field (free-form), state of registration as a short text field where respondents enter a US state name or two-letter state code (short_answer type, no hard character limit enforced but expect entries under 40 characters), tax-exempt status as a radio button choice with exactly two options labelled "Yes" and "No", and a text field for uploading or describing their tax certificate (short_answer type allowing a short description or file reference string).

When everything is done, call claim_done.

Task-Solving Rationable with Sub-task Decomposition:
To solve this task efficiently, the main agent freezes the complete audit computation into one canonical payload first, then dispatches exactly one wave of two parallel coder sub-agents (workbook writer and calendar/forms writer). No plan agent is used: the frozen payload and the two writer contracts below are the complete plan.

Dynamically resolve the workspace, read Tax_Regulations.pdf and guide.md, and freeze the exact state-rate/fallback methodology, the inclusive 0.50/1.00 classifications, the form wording/flags, and the four 2026 filing dates (April 15 "Tax Filing Deadline - Q1", July 15 "Q2", October 15 "Q3", January 15 "Q4"). Retrieve orders with perPage=100, increasing page to a short or empty page and omitting status; retrieve all tax rates to exhaustion. Preserve order ID, total, total_tax, billing state, and observed status. For each order sum all exact state-specific rates, using the summed empty-state default only if none exists; compute expected tax, actual tax, signed Actual-Expected, and classifications from unrounded values (abs<=0.50 Compliant with 0.50 inclusive; 0.50<abs<=1.00 signed Over-/Under-Collection with 1.00 on this boundary; abs>1.00 signed Over-/Under-Collection). Read the computation back and freeze one canonical audit_results.json in the workspace containing: all order audit records sorted by Order_ID ascending with 2-decimal monetary values and 4-decimal rates, the alphabetic State Summary rows with Compliance_Rate_Pct (1 decimal) and Requires_Filing (Yes when total actual tax exceeds $100), and the Compliance Overview metrics. This file is the single binding input for both sub-agents; after the freeze nobody re-reads the store, the rates, the PDF, or the guide.

1. Wave 1 — dispatch exactly 2 coder sub-agents in parallel, both consuming audit_results.json verbatim with no recomputation and no source-system reads:

   1. coder 0 (office-report-builder 0): Workbook writer — sole writer of Tax_Compliance_Report.xlsx. Create it exactly once with exactly three sheets: Order Tax Audit with columns Order_ID, Order_Total, Billing_State, Applicable_Rate, Expected_Tax, Actual_Tax, Discrepancy, Status and every order sorted by Order_ID; State Summary with columns State, Order_Count, Total_Revenue, Total_Expected_Tax, Total_Actual_Tax, Net_Discrepancy, Compliance_Rate_Pct, Requires_Filing sorted alphabetically; Compliance Overview with two columns Label and Value and the nine stated metrics. Write every value as a literal rounded number, never an Excel formula; read all three populated ranges back and return path, sheet order, row counts and equality controls.
   2. coder 1 (external-workflow-operator 0): Calendar/forms writer — sole owner of the external outputs. In native parallel, call list_events for each of the four filing dates with ISO midnight timeMin, next-civil-midnight timeMax, sufficient maxResults and orderBy="startTime", and filter exact title/date locally; create only missing reminders with start.dateTime="[filing-date]T00:00:00" and end.dateTime="[next-civil-date]T00:00:00" (all-day, description "Quarterly tax filing deadline reminder"), omitting timeZone unless the regulations provide one, and retrieve each retained ID with get_event. Forms has no list/search: call create_form exactly once titled Vendor Tax Information, never retry an ambiguous failure, then append sequentially in exact task order three add_text_question calls (vendor name, tax ID, state of registration), one add_multiple_choice_question with options ["Yes","No"] for tax-exempt status, and one add_text_question for the certificate description/file-reference field, copying required flags exactly; call get_form and verify title, five-question order, types, options, wording and flags.

After Wave 1, verify both handoffs in one single pass against audit_results.json: workbook cell-for-cell, four exact event identities, and the five-question form structure. Accept only after every read-back matches the frozen payload, then call claim_done. Do not dispatch any further agent after Wave 1.

TASK: Create three all-day quarterly tax filing deadline reminder events on Google Calendar for the year 2026. One event ("Tax Filing Deadline - Q1" on 2026-04-15, id 9bc4f1bd-7d31-41fa-a781-d2a01a1a6f0c) has ALREADY been created by me — do not modify, delete, or duplicate it.

CONTEXT: A finance team is running a tax compliance audit for an online store. The store's Tax Regulations PDF defines quarterly filing deadlines (Q2 = Apr-Jun → July 15; Q3 = Jul-Sep → October 15; Q4 = Oct-Dec → January 15). Reminders must be all-day events on the calendar, all in 2026.

TOOLS: Use only mcp__google_calendar__create_event, mcp__google_calendar__get_event, and mcp__google_calendar__list_events. Do not use any other tools or touch any files.

CREATE EXACTLY THESE THREE EVENTS:
1. Title: "Tax Filing Deadline - Q2" — all-day on 2026-07-15
2. Title: "Tax Filing Deadline - Q3" — all-day on 2026-10-15
3. Title: "Tax Filing Deadline - Q4" — all-day on 2026-01-15

EXACT RECIPE (this exact format already worked for the Q1 event): call create_event with the summary above, start = {"dateTime": "YYYY-MM-DD"} (date-only string, no time component), end = {"dateTime": "<next calendar day>"} . Specifically:
- Q2: start {"dateTime": "2026-07-15"}, end {"dateTime": "2026-07-16"}
- Q3: start {"dateTime": "2026-10-15"}, end {"dateTime": "2026-10-16"}
- Q4: start {"dateTime": "2026-01-15"}, end {"dateTime": "2026-01-16"}
This produces events spanning the full day from midnight to midnight (all-day). Do NOT add descriptions, locations, attendees, or recurrence. Titles must match exactly, including the " - " separator (space hyphen space) and capitalization.

VERIFICATION: After creating all three, call list_events for the range 2026-01-01 to 2026-12-31 and confirm there are exactly FOUR tax filing deadline events total (the existing Q1 plus your three), each with the correct title and date. Do not create any other events. If a create call fails, report the exact error — do not retry with a different date format and do not create duplicates.

DELIVERABLE (report back): the three new event IDs with their exact titles and start/end as returned, plus confirmation that exactly four deadline events exist in 2026.
Create remaining 3 calendar events

TASK: Create a Google Form titled "Vendor Tax Information" to collect tax details from a store's vendors, with exactly five questions.

CONTEXT: A finance team is running a tax compliance audit and needs to collect tax information from vendors via a Google Form.

TOOLS: Use only mcp__google_forms__create_form, mcp__google_forms__add_text_question, mcp__google_forms__add_multiple_choice_question, and mcp__google_forms__get_form. Do not use any other tools or touch any files.

STEPS:
1. Create exactly ONE form with the title exactly "Vendor Tax Information" (you may add a short description such as "Please provide your tax details for our compliance records."). Do NOT create more than one form under any circumstances.
2. Add exactly these five questions, in this order:
   a. Short-answer (text) question, title: "Vendor Name" — free-form single-line answer, not required.
   b. Short-answer (text) question, title: "Tax ID Number" — free-form single-line answer, not required.
   c. Short-answer (text) question, title: "State of Registration" — respondents will enter a US state name or two-letter state code; plain short-answer text type with no character limit, not required.
   d. Multiple choice (radio) question, title: "Tax-Exempt Status" — with EXACTLY two options in this order: "Yes" and "No". No other options. Not required.
   e. Short-answer (text) question, title: "Tax Certificate (Upload or Description)" — allows a short description or a file reference string; plain short-answer text type, not required.
3. Use add_text_question for questions a, b, c, e and add_multiple_choice_question for question d. For d, the options array must be exactly ["Yes", "No"].
4. Verify with get_form that the form title is exactly "Vendor Tax Information" and that it contains exactly 5 questions with the correct titles, types, and options.
5. If any add-question call fails, do NOT create a second form — instead report exactly which step failed and the error message.

DELIVERABLE (report back): the form ID, the responder URI / edit URI if available, and the list of the 5 questions exactly as confirmed by get_form (titles, types, options).
Create Vendor Tax Information form
